summary:
MARS-X is a 3D web simulator designed to explore a real area of Mars—Jezero Crater—and virtually test how a person or different types of vehicles (solar or nuclear-powered) would travel across it. It serves as a preliminary testing ground to study and compare Martian routes before planning more complex missions.

How It Works and What You Can Do
The system processes public Mars maps and imagery (including data from the Perseverance rover) to build a three-dimensional environment with layers for terrain, soil, and weather conditions. On the web interface, users select a starting point, a destination, and a traveler type. The tool then calculates routes by factoring in terrain slope, available energy, or communication challenges, while also allowing users to test their own custom algorithms.

Scope and Limitations
Technically, it combines an interactive web map with analysis tools that share standardized data formats to save and review results. However, MARS-X is strictly a conceptual exploration tool: it does not control real vehicles, simplifies certain physical conditions, and does not certify that a path is safe for an actual mission. It was independently created for the NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge.
details:
MARS-X is a 3D web simulator that uses public Mars data (including Perseverance rover observations of Jezero Crater) to test how astronauts and solar- or nuclear-powered rovers navigate Martian terrain.

How It Works & Key Benefits Users select a start point, destination, and traveler type on an interactive 3D map. The platform calculates optimal routes by factoring in slope, energy constraints, weather, and communication limits, while allowing users to test custom pathfinding algorithms. Its main benefit is offering a fast, accessible sandbox to compare mission strategies and save standardized test results before committing to complex, high-cost simulations.

Creativity, Factors & Impact Built with web mapping technologies and data-processing scripts, MARS-X creatively bridges raw planetary datasets with an intuitive, playable testbed. Our team prioritized real-world environmental constraints—such as terrain inclination, power sources, and signal blackouts—alongside clear data transparency (distinguishing real measurements from simulated layers). Ultimately, MARS-X aims to democratize space mission planning, empowering students, researchers, and enthusiasts to explore Martian logistics safely and collaboratively.
